nodes.label: error-driven-repair-loop

Loop protection stops on MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_GAP=3, on a repeated error_signature+code_hash pair, and scopes both to the verifier version that produced the verdict.

Every match names the registry row that answered and records every candidate that did not; a resolution that no registry supports returns NO_EXISTING_CAPABILITY rather than a guess. nodes.label: control-workspace-resilience

Unmeasured probes (write paths deliberately not fired) leave the denominator rather than counting as healthy, so a fully dead Core reads OFFLINE and not DEGRADED. A corrupt snapshot is an expected state (SNAPSHOT_INVALID) that opens an empty shell instead of crashing. Loopback failures are classified as LOCAL_SERVICE_DOWN without consulting the internet, and an external failure is separated from an internet failure by a real reachability probe, so losing the internet never marks a local DNA OS service DOWN. Undeliverable outbound work enters a disk-backed queue keyed by destination+payload_hash; retries back off exponentially to a 5-minute ceiling and stop at MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 (EXHAUSTED) or immediately on AUTH_FAILURE/INVALID_CONTRACT/PERMISSION_DENIED (FAILED_PERMANENT), both demanding incident evidence. A terminal record can only be revived by an explicit reset, so re-submitting the same work cannot reset the attempt counter.

Each accepted event becomes exactly one EngineMessage on the CoreBus carrying its own correlationId, and the replyToken is retained per user so a reply can be sent back on the same conversation. It executes nothing itself: it is an ingress boundary that turns a verified external message into an internal one.

Admin endpoints under app/api/admin/line-customers/[lineUserId]/ send a document or a debt notice back to one identified customer, which is the return leg of the Owner's LINE workflow. nodes.label: business-document-issuance

nodes.label: debt-and-payment-tracking
nodes.purpose: track_what_is_owed_and_reconcile_it_against_real_bank_evidence: debt events are recorded per party and carry their own lifecycle, with a dedicated route that issues a receipt when one is settled. Reconciliation is evidence-driven rather than declared: bank notification emails and bank statement transactions are ingested by their own Edge Functions and swept against receipts, so a payment is matched to real bank data instead of being marked paid by hand. A scheduled reminder function chases what remains outstanding. This capability was reported as MISSING on 2026-09-02 before the source pointers were followed; it is not missing.

nodes.label: business-entity-registry
nodes.purpose: hold_the_identity_of_the_business_parties_the_other_capabilities_refer_to: company/person identity is stored once in entity_registry and linked outward — company_line_links binds a LINE identity to a business entity, pit_profiles carries the counterparty profile, and conversation_states keeps where a given conversation has reached. Every other business capability refers to a party through this registry rather than keeping its own copy, which is what makes a LINE message, a document and a debt refer to the same customer.

nodes.label: expense-ingestion
nodes.purpose: normalize_one_billing_email_into_one_expense_without_guessing_what_it_does_not_say: the vendor is derived from the real sender domain, so there is no vendor allow-list to maintain and an unseen provider still normalizes. Anything the email does not state — amount, currency — becomes UNKNOWN with a reason recorded in extraction_reasons rather than an inferred number. Deduplication is by source_message_id, so one Gmail message can only ever become one expense.

nodes.label: claude-execution-boundary

The two privileges machine auth requires — exec /usr/bin/security and read ~/Library/Keychains — exist only in this boundary's own profile and are proven to remain denied to the general Agent sandbox. nodes.label: control-workspace-resilience
nodes.purpose: render_shell_before_backend_then_label_every_value_with_its_age: the screen opens with no backend call above it, fills from a disk snapshot labelled ORIGIN=SNAPSHOT/AS_OF/STALE_AGE_MS, then reconciles against backend truth by stable id and patches only what differs — never a full page reload. Unmeasured probes (write paths deliberately not fired) leave the denominator rather than counting as healthy, so a fully dead Core reads OFFLINE and not DEGRADED. A corrupt snapshot is an expected state (SNAPSHOT_INVALID) that opens an empty shell instead of crashing. Loopback failures are classified as LOCAL_SERVICE_DOWN without consulting the internet, and an external failure is separated from an internet failure by a real reachability probe, so losing the internet never marks a local DNA OS service DOWN. Undeliverable outbound work enters a disk-backed queue keyed by destination+payload_hash; retries back off exponentially to a 5-minute ceiling and stop at MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 (EXHAUSTED) or immediately on AUTH_FAILURE/INVALID_CONTRACT/PERMISSION_DENIED (FAILED_PERMANENT), both demanding incident evidence. A terminal record can only be revived by an explicit reset, so re-submitting the same work cannot reset the attempt counter.

nodes.label: ui-verification-runner
nodes.purpose: Deterministic UI verification runner. DNA OS invokes it; it drives a real browser over the DevTools Protocol and returns PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED computed only from machine values (bounding boxes, computed styles, console entries, network responses). No model decides any status; screenshots are evidence pointers only. Releases the browser and temporary profile on every exit path.

nodes.label: system-map
nodes.purpose: DNA OS surface map and smallest-sufficient-scope resolver. Resolves an Owner intent to the exact owning files from a declared map instead of letting an agent scan the repository; an intent that names neither a route nor an element returns SCOPE_UNRESOLVED rather than falling back to a full scan. Also holds the per-route expected values (such as visible heading count) that make deterministic correctness a system fact backed by source evidence rather than an Owner decision.

nodes.label: verification-dispatch
nodes.purpose: DNA OS-owned verifier selection and invocation. Classifies a change from its paths, looks the verifier up in the canonical registry (refusing to select one that is not REGISTERED), invokes it, and translates the machine result into the evidence the existing completion gate already reads. Callers cannot name a verifier or choose the check set.

nodes.label: remote_mcp.invoke_tool
nodes.purpose: Provider-neutral remote MCP execution boundary owned by DNA OS. It resolves the endpoint from the resource row in the canonical registry rather than from the caller, accepts only a credential_ref (never a token), and performs every eligibility check — resource registered, endpoint remote, read/write class permitted, credential present and ACTIVE — before any network request is made, so a denied invocation is provably network_request_made=false. It reconciles the remote tools/list against the registered capability and refuses with RESOURCE_CONTRACT_DRIFT rather than calling a tool the remote no longer declares. It knows no provider as a business rule and never receives, stores, or logs a secret.

nodes.label: owner.human_verify
nodes.purpose: Real human verification of the machine owner. A tiny Swift helper asks macOS to evaluate LAPolicy.deviceOwnerAuthentication, so the system shows its own Touch ID dialog with a password fallback and DNA OS receives only success or failure — never a password, a fingerprint, or anything from the Secure Enclave. It replaces the previous practice of treating a console-username match as authentication, which any process running as the owner could satisfy. A challenge is single-use, expires, is bound to its own id, and is refused if the console owner changes mid-flight; when the helper is unavailable the answer is UNAVAILABLE, never a fallback to the presence check.

nodes.label: owner.auth_session.mint
nodes.purpose: Mints a trusted owner session only from a challenge that macOS itself verified, and only while the console owner still matches. Presence is a necessary precondition, never a sufficient one; a session cannot be produced from a console username alone. Each challenge mints at most one session and is marked CONSUMED, so a replay is refused rather than honoured.

nodes.label: joint-resolver
nodes.purpose: The MATCH stage that answers whether any code needs to be written before anyone writes it. It reads only the canonical registry and the credential registry, never a model and never an agent's prose. A capability the registry already provides with a live credential resolves DIRECT_MATCH with code_generation_required=false; the same capability without a usable credential resolves AUTH_REQUIRED rather than being mistaken for missing; a declared composition whose parts are all registered resolves COMPOSITION_MATCH and reuses them; anything unknown resolves MISSING rather than being matched to something merely similar.

nodes.label: mcp-export-policy
nodes.purpose: Deterministic export policy for the DNA OS MCP server. Discovery and invocation are separate permissions, so a caller without rights does not even learn that a control-plane tool exists. Every tool defaults to INTERNAL_ONLY with a verified-owner-session requirement, which means a tool added later and left unclassified is closed rather than open. The three mutating tools (submit_command, submit_registration_candidate, submit_work_result) are OWNER_ONLY and require an owner session that passed real macOS human verification; a requester identity string alone is never sufficient.

nodes.label: standard-surface
nodes.purpose: Provider-neutral surface contract and renderer. A module declares which surface type it needs and how to read its data; the renderer turns a definition plus already-normalized rows into a table, so a new view is a binding rather than a generated page. It imports no business module — the same renderer produced a DOCUMENT_LIST and a TABLE from one dataset with different column bindings and zero new code. A surface type without a real renderer returns UNSUPPORTED_TYPE instead of an empty result, and a field a row does not carry is omitted rather than filled with a blank, so the screen never invents data.

nodes.label: application-package
nodes.purpose: The first machine-readable DNA OS application package, BUSINESS_COMMUNICATION_AND_EXPENSE_INTAKE. It names required capabilities and surface bindings only; it holds no provider logic and no UI. Each module records its own runtime status from measured evidence rather than from the presence of source, so a module whose implementation exists but cannot currently run is carried as RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE and is not selected as if it were usable.
